rounds.diagnosis: The pour stage was infeasible because its PATH already demanded the finished pour orientation: 'teapot.front_axis antiparallel mug.up_axis, tol tight' must hold at every pose along the way. The stage, however, starts where the carry stage ends, with the teapot upright (front_axis horizontal, up_axis along world.z). No motion can go from upright to spout-down while staying inside a tight antiparallel band, so the path region excluded its own start and the planner found nothing. Freeing the path rotation row lets the pot rotate through the intermediate tilt angles while the subgoal row still enforces the final spout-down pouring orientation. The snug height band on the path also left almost no room for the spout tip to swing as the body rotates about the handle; widening that slack one step gives the tilting motion vertical room above the mug while the centered row keeps the spout over mug.opening_center and the subgoal still fixes the final pour height.

Re-emit the pour stage with a path rotation row that keeps the tilt in the pouring plane - e.g. teapot.+left (or -left) held perpendicular to world up / level - so the motion is a monotone forward tilt about the lateral axis with the spout opening always directed toward the mug.
